ass:cmh-recovery-envelope.description: Seek a regular moment-map approximation of every centered log-concave law with a dimension-free CMH bound.

ass:tight-prefix-carleson.description: Control the accumulated localization source by time, the remainder, and an absorbable share of damping.

ass:weighted-package.description: The historical covariance-weighted estimate for near-minimizing cuts; its universal claim was refuted.

cert:ambient-intrinsic-comparison.description: Package equality of ambient and intrinsic relaxed energies and Poincaré constants.

cert:binary-tensorization.description: Bound the Poincaré constant of two independent factors by the larger factor constant.

cert:finite-tensorization.description: Identify the constant of a finite independent product with the supremum of its factor constants, including degenerate cases.

cert:gaussian-one-dimensional.description: Identify a one-dimensional Gaussian's optimal Poincaré constant with its variance, including zero variance.

cert:legacy-relaxed-comparison.description: Transfer smooth-test bounds to relaxed-energy constants; this certificate does not identify Cheeger energy.

cert:linear-test-lower.description: Use linear tests to bound the Poincaré constant below by the largest covariance eigenvalue.

conj:kls.description: Seek one dimension-free Poincaré bound for all isotropic log-concave laws, equivalently a covariance-scaled bound.

cor:absolutely-continuous-relaxation-two.description: Identify canonical energy with twice Cheeger energy when the intrinsic law has a density, including log-concave laws.

cor:ambient-intrinsic-constant-equality.description: Show that ambient and intrinsic relaxed energies have the same optimal Poincaré constant, including infinity.

cor:cmh-recovery-sequence-suffices.description: Deduce KLS if every centered log-concave law has a regular recovery sequence with a universal CMH bound.

cor:conditional-fiber-twelve-bound.description: For full-dimensional log-concave laws, bound fiber energy by four times gradient energy; the historical ID retains “twelve”.

cor:tight-window-consumption.description: Turn the assumed tight-prefix estimate into a dimension-free boundary bound and then KLS.

def:affine-poincare-constant.description: Define the affine Poincaré constant using relaxed covariance-weighted gradient energy on the affine support.

def:affine-support-intrinsic-law.description: Describe the smallest affine space carrying the law and its probability distribution in intrinsic coordinates.

def:conditional-fiber-form.description: Define energy by averaging conditional variances along lines, normalized by each fiber's coordinate variance.

def:extended-energy.description: Define an energy that may be infinite and the domain where it is finite.

def:intrinsic-affine-energy.description: Transport relaxed smooth-gradient energy from intrinsic coordinates back to ambient L² classes.

def:isoperimetric-cheeger-scale.description: Define the Cheeger constant from boundary expansion relative to the smaller mass, and define its reciprocal scale.

def:isotropic-law.description: Define an isotropic law as centered with identity covariance, including the zero-dimensional case.

def:l2-energy-poincare-constant.description: Define the optimal variance-to-energy constant for an extended energy on L².

def:l2-mean-variance.description: Define mean, centering, and variance independently of the representative of an L² class.

def:legacy-smooth-test-poincare.description: Define the Poincaré inequality and its optimal constant using globally smooth tests with finite gradient energy.

def:literature-poincare-constant.description: Define the literature Poincaré constant using locally Lipschitz tests and local slopes on the affine support.

def:log-concave-law.description: Define log-concavity by the mass inequality for convex combinations of compact sets, allowing lower-dimensional support.

def:poincare-test-family.description: Define variance-to-energy quotients and their optimal bound on a specified test domain, with zero-energy conventions.

def:preenergy-relaxation.description: Extend a test energy by taking the least limiting energy among convergent test sequences.

def:selected-canonical-frontend.description: Choose intrinsic relaxed smooth-gradient energy as the canonical energy and define its Poincaré constant.

def:smooth-gradient-preenergy.description: Assign each admissible smooth function the integral of its squared gradient.

def:smooth-gradient-relaxation.description: Extend smooth-gradient energy to L² by sequential relaxation.

lem:affine-poincare-translation-invarian.description: Show that translating a log-concave law preserves log-concavity and its affine Poincaré constant.

lem:ambient-intrinsic-covariance.description: Identify ambient covariance with intrinsic covariance on the support and zero on normal directions, preserving the operator norm.

lem:conditional-fiber-energy-comparison.description: Turn an assumed fiber Poincaré bound with coefficient κ into a gradient-energy comparison and a κC global bound.

lem:conditional-fiber-form.description: Establish closed quadratic and Markov properties of the conditional-fiber energy under the stated density and moment assumptions.

lem:covariance-core-closure.description: Close the transformed gradient operator and identify its Lipschitz and smooth-core closures for log-concave densities.

lem:covariance-test-core-density.description: Approximate locally Lipschitz tests and their transformed gradients by compactly supported smooth tests under absolute continuity.

lem:finite-energy-factor-poincare.description: Transfer a Poincaré bound between energies when one is bounded by a finite multiple of the other.

lem:logconcave-intrinsic-absolute-contin.description: Show that a log-concave law has a density in its intrinsic affine space, even if singular in the ambient space.

lem:mutual-test-approximation-relaxation.description: Identify two relaxed energies when each test family approximates the other without increasing limiting energy.

lem:preenergy-poincare-relaxation.description: Show that sequential relaxation preserves valid Poincaré bounds and the optimal constant.

lem:relative-perimeter-cheeger-infimum.description: Identify the Cheeger infimum over Borel sets with the weighted-perimeter infimum over smooth domains.

lem:relative-perimeter-smoothing.description: Approximate a smooth-domain indicator by smooth Lipschitz functions whose limiting gradient integral is at most its perimeter.

lem:smooth-tests-affine-restriction-exte.description: Restrict smooth tests to the affine support and extend intrinsic tests back while controlling gradient energy.

obs:dirac-raw-energy.description: Exhibit two functions equal for a Dirac law whose raw gradient energies differ, explaining the need for relaxation.

obs:normal-direction-raw-energy.description: Show that a function vanishing on the affine support can still have positive ambient gradient energy in a normal direction.

prop:spectral-sufficiency.description: Deduce a dimension-free Poincaré bound from the assumed full-damping occupation estimate.

prop:weighted-spectator-obstruction.description: Use independent exponential factors to refute the historical weighted package, without refuting KLS.

q:conditional-fiber-frame.description: Seek a frame independent of the test function that controls variance by fiber energy with a universal constant.

q:mm-spectral-occupation.description: Seek a universal-time source estimate for a fixed eigenfunction along localization, uniform through regular approximation.

q:smooth-gradient-raw-core-agreement.description: Determine when raw energy descends to L² and how sequential approximation relates to graph-norm density.

thm:affine-covariance-relaxation-closed.description: Identify the relaxed covariance energy of a log-concave law with the closed affine form used by the CMH route.

thm:affine-isotropic-reduction.description: Show that isotropic, covariance-scaled, and affine-energy KLS bounds are equivalent, including lower-dimensional laws.

thm:ambient-intrinsic-relaxation-equalit.description: Show that ambient and intrinsic smooth-gradient relaxations agree on the same L² space.

thm:borell-logconcave-density.description: Represent a log-concave law by an intrinsic log-concave density, positive with locally bounded reciprocal inside its convex support.

thm:cmh-recovery-affine-poincare-bound.description: Bound the affine Poincaré constant of a W₂ limit by the limiting CMH constants of a regular recovery sequence.

thm:compact-borell-logconcavity-equivale.description: Show that compact-set log-concavity is equivalent to the Borel-set formulation using inner measure.

thm:intrinsic-affine-constant-order.description: Characterize a valid intrinsic-affine Poincaré bound by comparison with the optimal extended constant.

thm:intrinsic-affine-energy-closed.description: Establish that intrinsic relaxed energy is a densely defined closed quadratic energy on ambient L².

thm:intrinsic-l2-equivalence.description: Identify ambient and intrinsic L² spaces by inverse linear isometries.

thm:klartag-density-frontend-identificat.description: Identify the intrinsic Cheeger constant with the smooth-boundary density formulation for non-Dirac log-concave laws.

thm:l2-energy-holds-order.description: Show that an L² energy inequality holds at a finite constant exactly when the optimal constant is no larger.

thm:legacy-canonical-constant-comparison.description: Identify the smooth-test, ambient relaxed, and canonical intrinsic Poincaré constants.

thm:legacy-relaxed-holds-equivalence.description: Show that smooth tests and ambient relaxed energy admit exactly the same finite Poincaré bounds.

thm:logconcave-cheeger-poincare-comparis.description: Prove both numerical comparisons for every finite-dimensional log-concave probability law: C_P^lit(mu) <= 4 Psi_KLS(mu)^2 and Psi_KLS(mu)^2 <= pi C_P^lit(mu). The exact pi Buser half now passes from actual smooth Gaussian convolutions through a finite Cheeger test bound under setwise convergence, Poincare upper stability, and intrinsic-coordinate transport. Zero-dimensional affine support and extended optima are included. This proves the numerical Cheeger-Buser comparison, not dimension-free KLS or individual-domain relative-perimeter convergence.

thm:one-dimensional-logconcave-poincare.description: Bound a one-dimensional log-concave law's Poincaré constant by four times its variance, including zero variance.

thm:quadratic-relaxation-closed.description: Show that relaxing a quadratic pre-energy with dense linear realization gives a closed quadratic form.

thm:selected-literature-constant-equival.description: Identify canonical and local-slope Poincaré constants for finite-dimensional log-concave laws.

thm:smooth-gradient-quadratic-dense.description: Show that smooth-gradient pre-energy is quadratic and its test realizations are dense in L².

thm:smooth-gradient-raw-core-agreement-d.description: Under explicit positive-density and local reciprocal bounds, identify intrinsic raw energy with its relaxation on the smooth core.

thm:smooth-gradient-relaxation-closed.description: Establish closed quadratic structure and a dense finite-energy domain for ambient relaxed gradient energy.

thm:smooth-gradient-relaxation-dirichlet.description: Show that normal contractions decrease relaxed gradient energy, giving the ambient and intrinsic energies the Dirichlet property.

thm:smooth-gradient-relaxation-two-cheeg.description: Identify canonical energy with twice local-slope Cheeger energy for every Borel probability law, including singular laws.

thm:smooth-lipschitz-constant-equivalenc.description: Identify smooth-test and locally Lipschitz Poincaré constants when the intrinsic law is absolutely continuous.

diagram:BV.description: Metric BV perimeter and half-mass Cheeger interfaces on the actual closed intrinsic support are defined. Complement symmetry is formalized for finite Borel measures on metric spaces, including the closed intrinsic support law; the zero-dimensional convention and an infinite-measure counterexample are proved. The half-mass and symmetric BV Cheeger constants are proved equal on every probability metric space. For a finite measure, globally Lipschitz approximants converging in global L1 may replace bounded-support tests and bound the perimeter, and on a proper metric space so may locally Lipschitz approximants (even under L1 convergence on every closed ball only, through clamping), the relaxation infima over both classes being equal to the perimeter (finite measures; the locally Lipschitz class on proper spaces with global or compact-set L1 convergence, in particular on the closed intrinsic support of every finite-dimensional law); epsilon recovery tests exist below every threshold above the perimeter, and every finite perimeter is the limit of the costs of an explicitly selected approximating sequence (for any Borel measure; nothing is claimed for infinite perimeter); the perimeter is sequentially lower semicontinuous under global L1 convergence of measurable set indicators for every Borel measure; for every probability law on a normed group it is at most the outer Minkowski content of every measurable set (one inequality, via two-radius plateau ramps), and the Minkowski coarea inequality holds with the actual local slope for every globally Lipschitz function, bounding the integrated superlevel content and BV perimeter of every test by its cost; every test has a quantitative superlevel selection with content at most cost/(1-2 delta) + epsilon and indicator error at most its L1 error over delta. For every set of finite BV perimeter, explicit measurable superlevel sets converge to it in L1 with Minkowski contents converging to its perimeter (Minkowski recovery), and the relaxed lower Minkowski content, the infimum of liminf outer contents over measurable sets converging in L1, equals the perimeter for every set; for measurable sets of mass strictly between 0 and 1 the recovery masses converge, eventually stay in (0, 1), and the symmetric Cheeger quotients converge to the BV quotient. The symmetric and half-mass BV Cheeger constants equal the Minkowski Cheeger constant for every probability law on a normed space, and for the intrinsic coordinate law they equal the isoperimetric constant (an equality of infima; the pointwise reverse inequality is false in general). Restriction to the closed measure support does not increase the metric BV perimeter of the trace of a set (one inequality, via restricted tests and the isometric-inclusion slope bound), with equality under an actual nonexpansive retraction onto a full-mass measurable subset, in particular, via the nearest-point projection, for every probability law on a Hilbert space with convex closed support, where the half-mass and symmetric BV Cheeger constants of the law and of its closed-support law agree. For every finite-dimensional log-concave probability law, the BV Cheeger constant on the closed intrinsic support therefore equals the isoperimetric constant. The upper Minkowski content, the limsup of the same radius quotient, is at least the lower content; for every set the real mass of its open s-thickening is monotone, hence differentiable at Lebesgue-almost every radius, and at every differentiability radius the upper content of that thickening is at most the derivative (probability laws on normed groups; no absolute continuity of the radius mass, integrated bound or lower-to-upper identity is claimed). This ✓ covers exactly that log-concave (convex-support) identification for the bounded-support relaxation; L1_loc convergence beyond proper spaces with finite measures, the literature relaxed Minkowski content theorem in general metric measure spaces, nonconvex supports, general metric-measure/RCD comparisons, the Buser route beyond existing proofs and dimension-free KLS are not claimed.

diagram:DECAY.description: For the actual full-dimensional log-concave weighted-gradient heat semigroup, an explicit positive form-domain Poincare constant C implies centered L2 squared-norm decay exp(-2t/C) for every L2 datum and t >= 0. Half-time self-adjointness gives centered indicator correlation at rate exp(-t/C), including null/full sets and zero time. The closed unit-gradient form optimum equals the intrinsic literature Poincare constant; a positive finite literature upper bound now supplies the gap. The Markov indicator L1/correlation identity feeds the smooth-model pi Buser proof. Arbitrary nonsmooth-law pi passage remains open.

diagram:GAUSS.description: For every finite-dimensional real inner product space, including dimension zero, every Borell probability density and every positive inverse variance, the actual normalized Gaussian convolution density and its negative logarithm are C-infinity. Each finite Gaussian-kernel derivative is uniformly bounded, allowing iterated dominated differentiation under the source probability law without source moments. Poincare stability and the Cheeger-infimum passage are separately proved bridges; no individual-domain perimeter limit is claimed.

diagram:GSTAB.description: For every Borell probability density on a finite-dimensional real inner product space, including dimension zero, the intrinsic literature Poincare optimum of its actual normalized Gaussian convolution is at most the source optimum plus 1/(2s) for s > 0. The proof identifies the Gaussian factor by its characteristic function and transports smooth-test bounds through product and convolution; it handles infinite optima without source moments or attainment assumptions. Together with the Cheeger test stability bridge, this yields general nonsmooth pi Buser; individual-domain perimeter convergence is not asserted.

The 2026-09-23 form-range continuation (Analysis/WaveSplitting/Potential.lean, KLS/LogConcave/HeatSemigroup/FormRange.lean) proves the class-level density of the form range: for nu = m.tilted(-U) log-concave with smooth U, T the closed unit-weight gradient, A = T*T and J = I + A, every z in D(T) and eps > 0 admit q in C_c^infty with [q] in D(A), J[q] in D(T) and sqrt(norm(J[q] - z)^2 + norm(T J[q] - T z)^2) < eps (exists_toLp_add_adjointComp_graph_lt; Dense form dense_formRange_graphL2 in graphL2 T). The bridges are proved: in any orthonormal basis sum_j (D_j f)^2 = norm(grad f)^2, sum_j D_j D_j f = Delta f, sum_j b_j D_j f = <grad U, grad f>, formOperator = f - L f, Z = int exp(-U) dm > 0 with int exp(-U) g dm = Z int g dnu, the norm bridge norm([f])^2 + norm(T[f])^2 = FE_w(f)/Z and the operator bridge J[q] = [q - L q] in D(T). Zero dimension is included (J = I). Two-field convergence and the arbitrary-data heat-test frontend remain open. See research/decisions/2026-09-23-wave-splitting-form-range.md. The time interpolation s -> int (P_s phi) Gamma(T(P_(t-s) f)) dnu, gradient estimates, general-law passage and small-time bounds remain open. See research/decisions/2026-09-23-heat-test-extension-frontend.md. The 2026-09-23 square-estimate continuation proves the time interpolation r -> int (P_(t-r) phi) Gamma(T P_r f) dnu with the outer semigroup on the test function, its right time derivative (tested weak-Gamma product rule with uniformly bounded difference quotients, L2/L1 pairing by truncation, generic time derivatives of P_t f and of the gradient orbit T P_t g, the difference bound |P_h psi - psi| <= h sup|A psi|) and its monotonicity via the heat-test frontend, hence the integrated square gradient estimate HeatSemigroup.integral_mul_weakGamma_le: int phi Gamma(T P_t f) dnu <= int (P_t phi) Gamma(T f) dnu for every f in D(T), t >= 0 and nonnegative phi in C_c^infty, smooth convex U (HeatSemigroup/GradientEstimate.lean, Generated/TimeDerivative.lean). Not proved: a pointwise a.e. form, the L1 self-improvement |T P_t f| <= P_t |T f|, the reverse BGL estimate, small-time bounds, the general-law passage and the constant pi. See research/decisions/2026-09-23-heat-gradient-square-estimate.md. The 2026-09-23 reverse-Poincare/self-improvement continuation proves, for smooth convex U, unit weight and nonnegative phi in C_c^infty, the reverse local Poincare (BGL, K = 0) inequality 2t int phi Gamma(T P_t f) <= int (P_t phi) f^2 - int phi (P_t f)^2 for arbitrary f in L2 and t > 0 (HeatSemigroup.two_mul_integral_mul_weakGamma_le; bounded data: 2t int phi Gamma(T P_t f) <= M^2 int phi) and Bakry's L1 self-improvement int phi |T P_t f| <= int (P_t phi) |T f| for f in D(T), t >= 0 (HeatSemigroup.integral_mul_norm_le). Inputs: Laplacian chain rule, improved Bochner |grad Gamma(f)|^2 <= 4 Gamma(f) Gamma_2(f), the pointwise sqrt(eps + Gamma) inequality, the regularized-norm calculus (Analysis/BakryEmery/RegularizedNorm.lean), the D(A) carre identity and the orbit derivative for arbitrary data. Not proved: a.e. forms, small-time BV bounds, general-law passage, the constant pi. See research/decisions/2026-09-23-heat-reverse-poincare-self-improvement.md. The 2026-09-23 a.e. continuation proves smooth-test order separation for integrable real functions on finite Borel measures (Analysis/TestFunctionOrder.lean), the bounded-data estimate |T P_t f| <= M/sqrt(2t) a.e. for t > 0 (HeatSemigroup.ae_norm_gradient_le_of_bounded), and |T P_t f| <= P_t |T f| a.e. for form-domain data and t >= 0 (HeatSemigroup.ae_norm_gradient_le), with global gradient L1 contraction (integral_norm_gradient_le). Small-time BV estimates, general-law passage and pi Buser remain open. See research/decisions/2026-09-23-heat-almost-everywhere.md. The 2026-09-23 small-time continuation proves integral |f-P_t f| <= sqrt(2t) integral |T f| on the whole form domain, L1 contraction between L2 inputs, and the smooth-domain relative-perimeter indicator estimate via the actual recovery sequence. The ENNReal endpoint includes infinite perimeter and zero time. This is not the sharp De Ponti-Mondino coefficient 2 sqrt(t/pi): their Gaussian-profile BGL estimate (32)-(33) is stronger than the proved ordinary reverse local Poincare inequality and remains open. See research/decisions/2026-09-23-heat-small-time-perimeter.md. The 2026-09-24 Gaussian scalar continuation constructs the actual Gaussian CDF/quantile profile and proves its ODE I I'' = -1 on (0,1), attained bound 1/sqrt(2*pi), endpoint limits, continuity and strict concavity on [0,1] (Probability/Line/GaussianProfile.lean). Regularized-profile calculus and the BGL heat interpolation remain next; no heat coefficient or route completion changes. See research/decisions/2026-09-24-gaussian-profile.md. The 2026-09-24 regularization continuation proves interior smoothness, reflection and midpoint normalization, shifted-profile nonnegativity, derivative bounds, Lipschitz control, a uniform value bound and pointwise epsilon convergence on [0,1). It constructs a globally smooth extension agreeing near the admissible interval, with bounded value and first two derivatives. A smooth-input weighted-Laplacian chain-rule client is proved. The tested D(A) generator chain rule and BGL heat interpolation remain next; heat constants are unchanged. See research/decisions/2026-09-24-gaussian-regularization.md. The 2026-09-24 tested-chain-rule continuation proves integrability and the scalar generator composition identity on arbitrary D(A) data for globally smooth Phi vanishing at zero with bounded value and first two derivatives, bounded psi in D(A), and a C1 potential (no A psi bound or convexity premise). The actual shifted Gaussian-profile specialization constructs and eliminates its extension under an explicit a.e. range margin. BGL heat interpolation, any needed stronger composition-domain identification and endpoint limits remain next; heat constants are unchanged. See research/decisions/2026-09-24-heat-chain-rule.md. The 2026-09-24 composition-domain continuation proves recognition from the actual smooth graph core and the operator chain rule when Gamma is in L2 (C1 potential). The positive-time bounded-data Gamma field is proved to be in L2 from the existing reverse bound. The shifted Gaussian operator frontend proves both range preservation and integrability from the initial range 0 <= f <= 1-2 eps, with no additional domain premise. Squared BGL interpolation, nonlinear time differentiation, endpoint limits and epsilon removal remain next; heat constants are unchanged. See research/decisions/2026-09-24-heat-composition-domain.md. The 2026-09-24 time-differentiation continuation proves scalar composition differentiation along L2 curves via affine quotients and Lipschitz perturbations, without asserting global Frechet differentiability of the composition map. The tested interior heat interpolation has derivative int P_s psi Phi'' Gamma, with exact generator cancellation for C1 potentials, bounded D(A) tests and arbitrary L2 data. The actual shifted Gaussian specialization has derivative -int P_s psi Gamma/I under the initial range margin. Its actual positive-time L2 derivative is also constructed. Squared BGL interpolation, its quantitative inequality and integration, endpoint limits and epsilon removal remain next; heat coefficients are unchanged. See research/decisions/2026-09-24-heat-composition-derivative.md. The 2026-09-24 strong-interpolation continuation proves the generated-semigroup product rule on varying differentiable data and its domain version. The shifted Gaussian interpolation has strong L2 derivative -P_s z with z=Gamma/I constructed in L2. Adding the heat-invariant I(eps) gives the unshifted positive profile, and bounded-test quadratic differentiation yields -2 int beta Y_s P_s z. Weighted semigroup Cauchy-Schwarz and L1 self-improvement for the quantitative dissipation bound, time integration, endpoints and epsilon removal remain next. Heat coefficients are unchanged. See research/decisions/2026-09-24-heat-strong-interpolation.md. The 2026-09-24 weighted-Cauchy continuation proves preservation of pointwise positive semidefinite two-by-two L2 matrices by positive real linear maps, using rational quadratic tests and continuity. Combined with L1 gradient self-improvement it gives the weighted square-gradient bound. The actual Gaussian specialization proves Gamma(T P_t f) <= Y_s P_s z a.e. and the quantitative tested square derivative <= -2 int beta Gamma(T P_t f), for bounded nonnegative tests in the smooth convex model with the initial epsilon range margin. Time integration, endpoints and epsilon removal remain next; heat coefficients and route markers are unchanged. See research/decisions/2026-09-24-heat-weighted-cauchy.md. The 2026-09-24 integrated-profile continuation proves strong continuity for varying semigroup data, including time zero, and continuity of bounded-test quadratic functionals. One fixed Gaussian interpolation curve on [0,t] gives the integrated tested inequality with both endpoints identified. L2 representative uniqueness and smooth-test order detection give 2t Gamma(T P_t f) <= I(P_t f+eps)^2 - (P_t I(f+eps))^2 a.e., with the actual initial profile constructed in L2. The smooth convex model, unit weight and epsilon range margin remain explicit. Removing that margin is next; the unregularized BGL estimate and improved heat constants remain open. See research/decisions/2026-09-24-heat-integrated-profile.md. The 2026-09-24 profile-limit continuation proves continuity of the Gaussian zero extension and dominated L2 convergence of I((1-2eps)f+eps). Exact heat and closed-gradient scaling, followed by bounded-test quadratic continuity, remove the epsilon range margin. For all 0<=f<=1 in L2 and t>0, the actual smooth convex unit-weight model satisfies 2t Gamma(T P_t f)<=I(P_t f)^2-(P_t I(f))^2 a.e., with I(f) constructed in L2. The integrated tested version is also proved. This completes the Gaussian BGL inequality in this model; deriving the improved bounded-data gradient and 2 sqrt(t/pi) L1/perimeter coefficients, general-law passage and pi Buser assembly remain next. KLS remains open. See research/decisions/2026-09-24-heat-profile-limit.md. The 2026-09-25 pi-coefficient continuation proves the unit-interval gradient bound 1/(2 sqrt(pi*t)) and the bounded-data bound M/sqrt(pi*t), including M=0. The dual time argument yields the 2 sqrt(t/pi) whole-form-domain L1 estimate, its form-approximation and recovery transfer, and the smooth-domain relative-perimeter bound in the actual smooth convex model. The ENNReal perimeter bound covers t=0 and infinite perimeter. Eight earlier public signatures are preserved as weaker bounds, and eight independent clients audit the new results. General-law passage, remaining perimeter interfaces, the form-domain-gap to literature-constant bridge and pi Cheeger-Buser assembly remain open; KLS remains open. See research/decisions/2026-09-25-heat-pi-coefficient.md.
